transcript.text: I had a gentleman who came 6 plus months
ago. Bought tickets months earlier, came
out here, took time away from the
business, and finally gets his chance to
have a question. And he says, "Hey Alex,
can you go through the closer
framework?" And I said, "Before I answer
the question, can you tell me what a
close rate is?" He says, "40%." So, you
went through all of that to have this
one opportunity to have an answer that
in no way will change your business.
A lot of times us as entrepreneurs, we
will focus on the thing that we enjoy
the most rather than the thing that the
business needs the most. And typically
the thing the business needs the most is
not the thing that you're the best at. A
lot of times our deficiencies translate
into the business efficiencies. And like
you can be unbalanced as an
entrepreneur, but the business can't be.
You will always be constrained by
whatever the weak link is in the
business, and that's fundamentally the
whole point of the theory of
constraints.
